title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity as contracts are awarded, missions launched, and new technologies emerge. Notably, funding for space resilience is on the rise, while commercial ventures continue to jockey for position in a competitive landscape.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The recent FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, indicating a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities. This influx of cash may bolster initiatives aimed at countering emerging threats in orbit.

themes.title: Commercial Launches Keep Coming
themes.body: SpaceX's CRS-34 cargo mission to the ISS underscores the ongoing reliance on commercial partners for resupply missions. Meanwhile, Virgin Galactic's commitment to begin commercial service this year suggests that space tourism is still very much alive, despite previous delays.

themes.title: International Collaborations on the Rise
themes.body: The joint ESA-China SMILE mission aims to deepen our understanding of Earth's magnetic shield, showcasing the potential for international partnerships in space research. This trend may signal a shift towards collaborative rather than competitive approaches in certain areas of space exploration.

themes.title: Hypersonic Developments Stumble
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped for the third consecutive quarter, raising questions about the pace of progress in this critical area. Such delays could have implications for national security and defense strategies that rely on advanced speed capabilities.
